name: Palazzo Cordusio, a Gran Meliá Hotel
positioning: Palazzo Cordusio Gran Meliá: the first Gran Meliá in Milan, in Luca Beltrami's 19th-century former Assicurazioni Generali headquarters on Piazza Cordusio, near the Duomo
best_for: Travelers who want a central Milan base near the Duomo, La Scala and the fashion district
Guests who want Duomo views from rooftop terraces or Sforza Castle views from a balcony room
Families who want children's services from the concierge, and guests travelling with pets

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Milan, near the Piazza del Duomo and the Quadrilatero della Moda fashion district.
The hotel is minutes from the Duomo and the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, with easy access to La Scala and the Castello Sforzesco.
The hotel is in the former headquarters of Assicurazioni Generali, designed in the 19th century by architect Luca Beltrami.
Luca Beltrami also designed Piazza della Scala and the restoration of the Castello Sforzesco.
The restored facade keeps its reliefs, including the lion of San Marco and a niche with an allegorical mosaic of Providence.
It is the first Gran Meliá hotel in Milan.
The hotel is a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
Rooms are decorated with Rubelli textiles.
The hotel offers a personalized butler service.
The concierge offers families children's services designed in partnership with FAO Schwarz Milano.
The hotel is pet-friendly, and pets receive a welcome gift.
Sachi, the hotel's Japanese restaurant, has a panoramic rooftop on the 4th floor with views of the Duomo.

highlights.text: The hotel has two rooftop terraces with views of the Duomo.
The spa has a large indoor pool, a gym, a sauna and a steam room.
Some rooms and suites have balconies overlooking the Sforza Castle.
The Duomo View Suite has a view of the cathedral and a separate living room.
The Cordusio Suite has a private terrace overlooking Piazza Cordusio and a living room with Molteni furniture.

considerations.text: Duomo and Sforza Castle views come with specific room and suite categories and the rooftop terraces, so pick the room type with the view you want.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning and prime location.
WhataHotel notes that historic building constraints may limit room size in some accommodations.
